content.text:
`src/instrumentation.ts` starts the in-process scheduler when the Node.js server starts. Every minute, `tick()` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` checks job cadences; when `digest-email` is due (at most once per hour), it queues the job and drains the queue. The queue dispatches it to `runDigestEmailJob()` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`. There is also an HTTP trigger: `POST` in `src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts` checks the cron secret and calls that same runner directly.

For each run, `runDigestEmailJob()` gets up to 50 organization IDs from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup()`, then loads each organization. `shouldRunForOrg()` skips archived organizations and selects an organization only when the current UTC hour equals its `settings.digestHourUtc`. The job also checks the `digest_email` feature flag with the organization’s plan and overrides. That flag is enabled from the growth plan upward by default, and an organization override can enable it.

For each eligible organization, `listDigestRecipients()` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts` delegates to `listDigestSubscribers()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`. That query returns distinct users with at least one preference row for that organization where `digestOnly` is true. It does not additionally require `email` to be true.

For each subscriber, the job sets a window from 24 hours before the run time through the run time, then calls `buildDigest()`. It rechecks the organization and feature flag, and asks `listUnreadSince()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts` for that recipient’s unread notifications in the organization created since the window start. `buildDigest()` excludes entries later than the window end, maps the remaining notifications to digest entries (kind, title, link, and creation time), and caps them at `DIGEST_MAX_ENTRIES`. The notification rows originate in `notify()` in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`, which is called by domain event listeners; it applies per-kind preferences, skips the actor, and inserts a row only if at least one channel remains.

When there are entries, the job loads the recipient with `findUserById()`, calls `renderDigest()`, and then `renderEmail("digest", …)` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` to produce the subject, HTML, and text. `sendEmail()` writes an `email.sent` record to the structured log; the service describes this as draft logging rather than outbound mail delivery. After sending, the job marks each included notification read, so it will not be included again in a later run. Failures during an individual recipient’s build, render, send, or mark-read steps are caught and counted in the job result.

A subscribed person can therefore receive no email that day if the organization is archived, its configured UTC digest hour has not arrived, or the digest feature is disabled. Even when the organization is due, no email is produced if the user no longer resolves, `buildDigest()` finds no qualifying unread notifications in the 24-hour window, or all candidate notifications were already read or lie outside the window. The notification fan-out can also omit a row entirely when the person is the actor or their preferences resolve to no channels; such activity cannot appear in the digest.
